diagnosis: HBV was calibrated on daily NSE over 1971-10 to 1997-12, after a 1-year warm-up, using DDS (about 6,500 runs in three stages). The soil store started at an equilibrium level of about 420 mm instead of the default 30 mm. Fit: NSE 0.889, KGE 0.905, r 0.943, PBIAS +3.2%, so the model slightly over-predicts flow volume. This is a rain-dominated, flashy Welsh border catchment. The fit came from fast upper-zone runoff (K0 about 0.98, UZL about 40 mm, K1 0.25, MAXBAS 1.5) and a fairly quick baseflow store (K2 0.08, PERC 3.9). The soil store is large (FC about 476 mm) with a steep, nonlinear recharge curve (BETA about 6.7) and LP about 0.87. Snow hardly matters (1.6% of precipitation falls as snow). The snow parameters (SFCF about 0.72, TT about 1) are therefore poorly identified and mostly act as small corrections to the water balance. Weak points: the largest flood peaks are probably under-predicted (max simulated 24.6 vs 45 mm/d observed). Low summer flows and the effect of FC/LP/BETA on drought recession are uncertain, and FC and BETA trade off against each other. Three DDS stages with different seeds ended at NSE values within 0.01 of each other. I am fairly confident about the response parameters and less confident about the soil and snow parameters. I did not test on a held-out period, so I expect NSE of about 0.83 to 0.88 for 1998-2008.
